recheck.evidence_quote: To get a token for your own account, go to Settings > Advanced, create an application, then click "Generate access token."
recheck.notes: Verified in part. Gumroad's own llms.txt lists https://gumroad.com/api as its REST API documentation (products, sales, subscribers, licenses). It also lists an official MCP/OAuth connector at gumroad.com/claude and gumroad.com/mcp, and help article https://gumroad.com/help/article/355-connect-ai-assistants-to-gumroad. The api page and help article 280 (https://gumroad.com/help/article/280-create-application-api) still fetch with only a title or heading, so the body text was not read directly. The quote above comes from search results for gumroad.com/api and the help center. It describes Settings > Advanced > create an application > Generate access token, with no mention of a fee or approval step. The base URL is https://api.gumroad.com/v2/. The API page covers products, categories, files, covers, emails, workflows, user and payouts. The sales endpoint path was not confirmed. Auth, inferred from the search summary: (1) a personal access token passed as the access_token parameter, with no app ID or secret needed; (2) OAuth2 for apps used by other accounts, with authorize at gumroad.com/oauth/authorize (client ID, redirect URI, scope) and token exchange at /oauth/token. The scope list is still unverified: view_sales is confirmed only by third-party sources. The Bearer header is not confirmed, so the token is documented as a parameter, not a header. This is a change to the current record's "Bearer token", which should be "access token (query/body parameter)". Moving to confidence medium: access is self-serve and free per vendor pages as summarized by search, but I did not read the full vendor page text.
